record.title: DrivingBench reports one successful low-speed physical-car course completion by GPT-6 Astra in a four-model evaluation
record.summary: A preprint and its authors’ benchmark site describe a closed-course test in which four general-purpose vision-language models controlled steering and speed in a 2022 Toyota Corolla through a 127 m cone course, using vendor-native agent harnesses and up to three attempts in one conversation. The authors report GPT-6 Astra was the only model to finish, on attempt 2; Claude Fable 5.1 reached 45% on attempt 3, while no other attempt passed 50%. The test used a human operator ready to brake, a single course and one evaluation session per model. The arXiv paper reports Astra’s finish at 4:44 after its first command, while the live site and attempt trace list 5:22; the timing difference is unresolved. This is evidence of a narrow author-reported physical-control result, not general road-driving ability or vehicle safety.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that, among GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-5.6 Sol and Grok 4.6, only Astra completed their 127 m low-speed cone course, doing so on its second attempt; Fable reached 45% on its third attempt and no other attempt passed 50%.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The benchmark gave each model up to three attempts in one continuous conversation and used a human operator in the vehicle, ready to brake; the tested result does not establish open-road performance or safety.

claims.label: CONTRADICTORY
claims.text: The paper states Astra reached the finish 4 minutes 44 seconds after its first command, while the current site leaderboard and trace list the attempt duration as 5 minutes 22 seconds; the difference in timing boundary is not resolved in the inspected sources.

contradictory_evidence: The arXiv paper says Astra reached the finish 4 minutes 44 seconds after its first command, while the live benchmark site and the attempt-2 trace list 5 minutes 22 seconds. The exact timing definition differs across the accessible pages and was not resolved in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent researcher has repeated the physical benchmark or audited the published raw traces and outcome calculation in this review.
The result covers one closed course and one session per model; reliability across maps, weather, lighting, vehicle models and repeated trials is unknown.
The paper’s 4:44 Astra completion time differs from the live site/trace duration of 5:22; the timing boundary remains unclear.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded result is accurate, a general-purpose vision-language model completed one real-car, closed-loop cone-course run after a prior attempt and reflection, extending evaluation beyond simulation and digital tasks. Its consequence is notable for physical-agent capability assessment, but evidence is one course and one same-context session per model, with no independent replication or general safety evidence.
limitations: The study evaluates four model/harness combinations on one course, with only one evaluation session per model; three attempts in the same conversation are not independent trials.
A human operator sat in the vehicle with a foot over the brake and could intervene; the setup was low-speed and on a closed lot.
The paper and current leaderboard/trace report different Astra finish durations (4:44 versus 5:22); the timing boundary was not resolved.
The course/map and cone placement were not fully surveyed; the authors note camera blind spots, actuator constraints and launch overshoot.
No independent reproduction, road test, crash-risk estimate, broad driving benchmark or safety validation was inspected.
brief.summary: A preprint and its authors’ benchmark site describe a closed-course test in which four general-purpose vision-language models controlled steering and speed in a 2022 Toyota Corolla through a 127 m cone course, using vendor-native agent harnesses and up to three attempts in one conversation. The authors report GPT-6 Astra was the only model to finish, on attempt 2; Claude Fable 5.1 reached 45% on attempt 3, while no other attempt passed 50%. The test used a human operator ready to brake, a single course and one evaluation session per model. The arXiv paper reports Astra’s finish at 4:44 after its first command, while the live site and attempt trace list 5:22; the timing difference is unresolved. This is evidence of a narrow author-reported physical-control result, not general road-driving ability or vehicle safety.

technical.claimed_result: The authors argue general-purpose frontier vision-language models can begin to act in the physical world and that physical-agent evaluation should account for latency, task framing and in-context adaptation. No general driving or safety claim is established.
technical.compute_or_cost: Published trace lists 5:22 and 6.6M tokens / $7.74 for Astra attempt 2. This cost depends on the listed model/harness pricing and does not measure deployment cost or driving efficiency.
technical.demonstrated_result: The authors report one successful Astra completion of a fixed low-speed cone course on its second same-context attempt among four evaluated models; Claude Fable 5.1 reached 45% on attempt 3 and the other attempts remained below 50%. These are author-reported measurements, not an independent replication.
technical.implementation_status: Research benchmark and open-source harness/report; not a deployed autonomous-driving system.
technical.mechanism: A model receives camera frames and speed/steering state through observe(), then issues timed steering and speed commands; the vehicle continues under a command while the model reasons, and later commands replace the current command. This makes perception, planning, actuation calibration and inference latency interact in closed loop.
technical.regime: 2022 Toyota Corolla, Comma 4/openpilot-based interface, 127 m closed parking-lot course, low-speed commands, cones, one model session per system and up to three sequential same-chat attempts; human operator remained ready to brake.
technical.reproducibility: Authors publish code, prompt, map, traces, video and telemetry; exact rerun requires a similar supported Toyota, Comma 4/openpilot setup and course. No independent physical rerun or artifact audit was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: The within-study comparisons use four named models in vendor-native harnesses on the same single course, with up to three attempts and retained conversation context. Harness differences and one session per model limit causal model ranking.

brief.title: DrivingBench reports one successful low-speed physical-car course completion by GPT-6 Astra in a four-model evaluation
brief.why_it_matters: The evaluation moves a general-purpose multimodal model from image interpretation to closed-loop action on a real vehicle, where latency and stale observations matter because the car continues moving while the model reasons. The result supports a constrained capability claim and makes harness, task framing and in-context reflection part of the measurement. A single low-speed course run with a human safety operator does not establish reliable driving or safe autonomy.
